title: Callout Marker Anatomy
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Interactive Infographic Overlays
Callout Markers
Leader Lines
Annotation-Free Illustration
Data-Driven Diagrams
description: A textless placeholder illustration of a sun, a mountain, and a lake carries three numbered markers, each joined by a leader line to a label outside the illustration. A table shows the x and y coordinate stored for each marker as a percentage of the image width and height. Dragging a marker updates its stored coordinate live, showing that marker position is data rather than pixels. A checkbox turns the leader lines on and off.

educational.topic: Stored marker coordinates, leader lines, and labels in an infographic overlay
learningObjectives: Explain how a stored marker coordinate, a leader line, and a label work together on an annotation-free illustration.
Explain why a marker position is stored as a percentage of the image size.
Describe how to correct a misplaced marker without regenerating the illustration.
prerequisites: Knows what an interactive infographic overlay and an annotation-free illustration are
Can read a small table of numbers

controls.label: Numbered marker
controls.description: Drag any of the three markers to a new position on the illustration; its stored x and y update in the table while it moves

controls.label: Label
controls.description: Selects that label's marker and highlights its row in the table

controls.label: Show leader lines
controls.description: Turns the leader lines between markers and labels on and off (on by default)

equations: x = (pointer x - image left edge) / image width x 100
y = (pointer y - image top edge) / image height x 100
assumptions: Coordinates are percentages from 0 to 100, measured from the top-left corner of the image, as in the overlay data.json format
The illustration is a placeholder drawn with shapes, not a generated image
limitations: Does not show the overlay engine's explore, quiz, or edit modes
Labels stay in a fixed order beside the illustration

pedagogical.pattern: Concrete data visibility with direct manipulation
pedagogical.teachingStrategy: The learner drags a marker and watches its stored value change, which makes the idea that position is data tangible
keyQuestions: What changes when a marker is dragged: the picture or the data?
What does a leader line add when a label sits outside the illustration?
commonMisconceptions: The labels and markers are part of the generated picture
A misplaced label can only be fixed by regenerating the image
assessmentOpportunities: Predict the coordinate that places a marker on a named feature, then check by dragging
